^"Guests," she said, without surprise. "Armed, wet, and trailing runaways. I like you already. Shall we trade?"

b: ^"Clever hands," she said. "Ashmoor? The miller there still owes me. Said he once had an apprentice who paid his debt in full. A rarity."

g-0: ^Her people were already laying out goods on the crates.
^Pay with a "favour" for what the silver won't cover.

c-1: ^"No matter," Renna smiled. "You'll owe me a favour. Which one, I'll tell you later. I always tell later."
^She lifted the lid of a crate holding the things that are never put out in the light.
^Irena silently watched you shake Renna's hand.
c-2: ^You counted out the silver. Renna counted it twice and nodded.

g-1: ^"Now to business," you said. "We need the sluice."

^"Everyone needs the sluice." Renna leaned back in her chair. "Through it you reach the old dwarven passages, and from there it's the surface or the very bottom, as you like. I'll let you through. The price is simple."
^She nodded at the fugitives huddled by the landing stage.
^"Them. The King pays by the head. Your heads I don't need, but theirs I very much do. You go through, they stay, everyone's happy. Almost everyone."

b: ^Mab said nothing. She was not looking at you, but at Garret.
^Tobin clenched his good hand into a fist, but said nothing.
^"You've left prisoners behind for speed before. The only difference is that these ones are looking you in the eye."
^"Think. The one you came here for is waiting below. And these... these may not make it anyway."

g-1: ^"Don't you dare," Irena said quietly. It was not to you, it was to Velior. But she was looking at you.
^Hand over the fugitives. Go through the sluice.

hand_over: ^You did not look at the fugitives while Renna's people tied them up. You looked at the water.

b: ^As Mab was led past, she stopped for a second in front of Garret.
^"You stood over us with a whip," she said. "Now you stand beside the one who's selling us. You haven't changed, Garret. You've just changed masters."
^Tobin did not resist. He only said, as he passed: "You promised," though you had promised nothing. Or had you.

hand_over: ^Irena turned to the wall and stood like that until the fugitives were taken away.
^"The bypass channel," said Renna, pleased. "My people will see you through. Mind, a few things swim in there. But you know how to deal with those."
^The channel met you with cold, and with movement in the water.
fight: ^Renna sighed, the way one sighs over a bad customer.
^The crossbowmen on the platforms raised their weapons. Behind you the fugitives grabbed whatever came to hand: planks, an oar, a length of broken pipe.

b: ^"At last," said Mab. "For once it's not just us."
^When it was over, Renna sat on the floor by her desk, tied up with her own belt, watching you with polite interest.
^"The office is through there," she said, before you asked. "Take what you like. I won't be trading any more anyway."
^The bypass channel brought you out at the back door of the pumping station. While Renna was upstairs counting her living goods, the office door stood unlocked.
^"Since we're here," said Velior, and went in first.

office: ^The office smelled of wax and dry paper. On the desk, under a heavy paperweight, lay a stack of letters.

letter: ^The top letter was unsigned, but no signature was needed. You knew the hand at once. Even, without a single blot, almost courteous. The same as on the "list".
^"To Mistress Sol. Terms as before: for each head, as agreed; for heads of the old houses, three times that, alive and unharmed. I enclose a register of the old houses for checking."
^Below it, a column of family names. In the middle: "Tal".
^And a postscript at the bottom, smaller:
^"Scout V., who compiled this register for me, has left my service. Do not touch him. He will come back of his own accord, once he understands he has nowhere else to go."
^Velior stood by the door. He had already read the letter over your shoulder; you could tell by his face. There was no joke in it.
^"Yes," he said, before you could ask. "It was me."

b: ^"And I did answer. You didn't ask the right way."
^"I asked you straight out. About the list. You said: scribes in the capital."
^"I was a scribe. One of them. Just a very good one."

letter: ^"He told me to find the old houses. The ones whose blood 'remembers'. I searched church books, gravestones, the songs grandmothers sing." Velior rubbed his burned cheek. "I found lines. I didn't know what he did with them. Then I found out. Then I left."
^"Tal." He did not look away. "Yes. It was hard. They hid well. Sixty years."
^"Tell me everything. Now. From the beginning."
^"Not here. We'll talk when we're safe."

confront_truth: ^Velior sat on the edge of the desk, as if his legs had stopped holding him.

^"The King saved me from the gallows. I was a thief and a tracker, and he said: you know how to find what people hide. Find me people. I found them. Twelve houses, in half a year. He was... grateful. He burned the crown into me with his own hand. I was proud."

^"And then I saw what was done to the ones I'd found. Not yours. Others, earlier." He fell silent. "I left that same night. Struck through the crown. And ever since I've been waiting for him to come for me. And he doesn't come."
confront_rage: ^You did not remember how you ended up next to him. You remembered only his throat under your fingers, and that he did not resist.
^Garret pulled you off him, grabbing you from behind.
^"Not like this," he said into your ear. "Not here. Not like this. Believe me, I know what it's like afterwards."
^"Fair," he wheezed. "I'd do the same in your place."
confront_wait: ^"Not here. We'll talk when we're safe. You'll tell me everything later."
^"Later," Velior repeated. "You're like Renna. Everything later." He smiled crookedly. "Fine. I'm not going anywhere. As you can see, I've nowhere to go."
reactions: ^"I knew he was lying," said Irena. "I didn't know about what."
^Garret was silent for a long time.
^"I carried a whip myself," he said at last. "Who am I to judge him. But it's your call. Maybe not now. But yours."
^You folded the letter and put it inside your shirt, next to the "list". Two papers, one hand.

projection: ^A narrow gallery above the water led to the sluice. Halfway along, Garret's lantern flickered and went out, though there was plenty of oil.

^In the dark above the water, light was gathering. Pale, like the glow of rotten wood. Slowly a figure emerged from it: a tall man in an old high-collared robe. The face could not be seen, only shadow and the glint of eyes.
^You knew the voice at once. The one from the dream. The one that kept the books.
^"So this is you," he said, studying you. "I have heard you described in different ways."
^You did not answer. Behind you the companions froze. Irena raised her staff, and the bell on it trembled without a sound.

^"Have no fear, sister. It is only light and water; I am far away." The figure turned its head slightly. "I simply grew curious. It is not every day that someone comes after me of their own accord. Usually I have to send for them."

b: ^"You chose rightly at the column," he told you. "Not everyone can. One's own is dearer than thirty-eight strangers. I understand. I thought so too. Once."
^"You freed the column and lost the cart," he told you. "Noble. I was noble once too. It passes."
^"And you paid Renna in the right coin. You see, you already know how to count."
^"You hear the whisper, don't you," he said more gently, almost like a teacher. "Do not fear it. It is more honest than people. I could teach you a great deal."

projection: ^"As for Velior..." He looked somewhere past your shoulder. "He searched well. Look after him. He will be useful yet. To us both."
^"I'm coming for you. And you'll regret it."

c-0: ^"I'm coming for you. And you'll regret not sending anyone to meet me."
^"You will come," he agreed. "You will come exactly where I need you. As for regret... oh, I have been regretting for sixty years. One more or one less."
c-1: ^The figure was silent for a long time.
^"To take back what was taken from me," he said at last. For the first time the voice was not courteous, only tired. "You will understand. One day you will understand better than anyone."
c-2: ^You said nothing. You simply looked, until he was the first to look away.
^"Silent," he said, with something like respect. "Rightly so. Words are cheaper than water here."
g-0: ^"I will not stand in your way," he said. "Go. You will come anyway."
^The light above the water broke apart like a reflection hit by a stone. Garret's lantern flared up again.
^"That was him," said Velior. His voice was a stranger's.

sluice: ^The sluice turned out to be a huge stone wall across the tunnel, with a gate of black iron. Above the gate runes were cut: angular, deep, plainly not human.

b: ^You could read one of them: "Hold". Just "hold". With no word on what.

sluice: ^At the foot of the gate, waist-deep in water, sat something large. At first you took it for a heap of rags. Then the heap raised its head.
^It was people. Several people, sewn into one body with thick wire, with a chain round its neck fixed to the gate. Someone had set it here on guard and forgotten it.
^"The dwarves never made that," Garret said quietly. "That's ours. That's from our workshops."
^The warden stood up, and water poured off it in streams.

after_fight: ^The warden sank into the water and went still. The chain slackened.
^Garret and Velior threw their weight on the gate lever together. The iron groaned, and the water began to drain: first in a thin trickle, then with a roar, into the blackness beyond the wall.
^When it was gone, a staircase opened behind the gate. Broad steps, cut for a short stride, went down towards carved arches.
^"The Dwarven Halls," said Velior. "I never went further than this. Not even on his orders."

camp2: ^Above the sluice there was a dry chamber, once a dwarven guardroom: stone benches, a niche for a fire, a sign cut into the wall: a hammer over a closed eye.
^Velior sat in the farthest corner, his back to the wall, and did not light a fire of his own.
^For the first time that day it was quiet.
^Before sleep you could talk to one of them.

fugitives_farewell: ^The fugitives were getting ready to make for the surface through old passages they knew of only from rumour. No food, two wounded to carry.
^"They won't make it on their own," Garret said quietly. "The passages are old, and there are guards up top."
^ is waiting below," said Velior. Not to you. To the side.
^See them to the runaways' camp above. Give them the silver from Renna's office.
fugitives_led: ^The way up took a day. Two rockfalls had to be cleared by hand, and the wounded were carried in turns. Renna's silver went on bread and blankets in the camp, down to the last coin.
^The camp turned out to be three fires in an old working right under the sky. People from the barracks already lived there. They met you as if they had been waiting.

b: ^"That's for the barracks," said Mab. "And for the pumping station. Now we're even. No. Now I owe you."
^She held out her hand to Garret. He looked at it for a long time before he shook it.
^"We'll tell everyone who brought us out," said Tobin. "Not 'let us go'. Brought us out."

fugitives_led: ^You went back down in silence. The day you had given away weighed on your shoulders heavier than the pack. Somewhere below,
^ had spent that day without you.
^But that night the whisper was silent. For the first time in a long while.
fugitives_parted: ^The fugitives said goodbye at the stairs.

b: ^"We'll wait for you up there," said Mab. "Or down here. Wherever it works out."
^She held out her hand to Garret. He looked at it for a long time before he shook it.
^"If we get out, we'll tell them who brought us out," said Tobin.
^"He said you already know how to count," said Irena. "The one above the water."
^"I prayed for them all the way through the channel. It was all I could do. It's very little."
^"He spoke to you as one of his own," said Irena. "The one above the water."
^"He was wrong," she said. "Today you didn't count the way he wanted. I saw it."
^"Mab was right," said Garret. "I haven't changed. I've just changed masters."
^For a long time he turned his cleaver over in his fingers.
^"Only now I choose the master myself. Maybe that's the difference. If there is one."
^"She shook my hand," said Garret. "Mab. Mine. I kept her in a cage for two years."
^He threw a broken pit prop on the fire.
^"I don't know what to do with that. Nothing, probably. Just remember it."
^Garret said nothing. He just threw a broken pit prop on the fire and watched it burn.

talk_velior: ^"In the morning, then. Everything in the morning." He turned to the wall. "You know what's funniest? He's right. I really have nowhere to go. Except with you."
leave: ^In the morning the stairs led down, towards carved arches and a silence many hundreds of years old.

b: ^The flooded storeroom. Nothing under the water but empty shelves.

ch2_nook_cellar: ^By the wall, just under the water, an opening showed dark. The door of a storeroom, its top edge barely above the surface. Beyond it, judging by the echo, it was dry, or almost.

ch2_nook_cellar_dive: ^The water closed over your head, black as ink. Three blind strokes, your hand found the edge of the doorway, one more stroke, and you surfaced in the dark, in a pocket of air under the vault.
^Once they had kept things here that they were afraid would get wet. The irony was not funny.

^On a hook right under the vault, where the water had not reached, hung a bundle in oiled leather. Inside was a cloak: dark, heavy, hooded, soaked in something that made water run off it like off a duck's feather.

^By the far wall, where the air ran out, a drowned man sat on a shelf. He had not risen with the others: he just stayed sitting, arms round his knees. Round his neck hung a waxed leather case, the kind couriers wear.
^You put the cloak on right over your wet clothes. This time the water seemed warmer.
^"A cloak of the underwater passage," said Velior, when he saw it. "Smugglers trade a boat for one of those. Where did you get it? No, don't tell me. I'll be hurt that I didn't find it myself."

b: ^The drowned man on the shelf. An empty case on a cord.

ch2_look_drowned_note: ^You took the case from the drowned man's neck. The wax had kept the water out.
^Inside the case was a note, dry.

^"If you find me: I went to the chapel by the sluice. The water there stands above the waist, but Father Meren used to say a candle still burns under the water. I want to see. If I don't come back, I saw."

b: ^A chapel under water. You had heard of such places: the first settlers built them when the mines were still small, and people asked the water not to come. The water came anyway.

ch2_look_drowned_note: ^A note in the journal: "The chapel by the sluice. Father Meren."

b: ^The end of the ledge. Old bedding, an empty quiver.

ch2_nook_ledge: ^At the far end of the ledge, behind the rocks, someone had once made a sleeping place: a sackcloth mat, a burnt-out candle, an empty flask. Whoever lived here had left long ago and not come back.
^Under the mat lay a bow. A good one, yew, with a leather wrap on the grip. On the limb a mark was burned: an ear of wheat and an arrow.
^You knew the mark. Old Hugo from Ashmoor marked his bows like that, the one who lived by the mill and grumbled at everyone who bought their bows in town.
^Someone from Ashmoor had been here before you. Maybe he went off to work before the dead came. Maybe not. You took the bow.

b: ^"The chapel by the sluice?" Mab smirked. "That's a story for the new ones. That there's a priest down there under the water with his fishing spear, and whoever goes down to him, he blesses. Or runs through. Depends what sort you are."

^"For fish. They say the first ones here didn't dig ore, they fished an underground lake. Blind white fish. The priest was their headman. With his spear he pinned the dead down in the water so they wouldn't rise." Mab paused. "An old woman told me that, in the barracks. She's dead now."

^"The chapel by the sluice?" Tobin rubbed his bandaged arm. "Heard of it. That there's a priest down there under the water with his fishing spear. They say the first ones here didn't dig ore, they fished an underground lake. The priest was their headman, and with his spear he pinned the dead down in the water so they wouldn't rise."
^"A week ago I didn't believe the dead walked." He shrugged. "Now I believe everything. It's simpler."

ch2_talk_fugitive_tale: ^A note in the journal: "A priest with a fishing spear. He pinned the dead down in the water."

b: ^The store under the platform. Empty crates.
^Under the platform stand crates with the smugglers' brand. All nailed shut, tightly and properly. Without tools and clever hands there's nothing to be done here.

ch2_nook_stash: ^Under the platform, in the dark between the piers, stood crates. Most held goods nobody cared about: salt, nails, cloth.

b: ^One crate was heavier than a crate of salt ought to be. You prised up a board with your knife.

^You raised the foreman's lantern. In its yellow light the salt in the cracks of the crates glittered, but in one it did not: under the salt there was something else. Garret prised up the board with his cleaver.
^"This one," Velior whispered, tapping one of the crates. "Too heavy for salt. Renna always keeps a stash where nobody will look: among things nobody wants."

ch2_nook_stash: ^Under a layer of salt lay a purse and two flasks of greater potion, packed in straw.

b: ^Irena looked at the purse, then at you.
^"You've already paid them," she said. "In people. You may as well take the silver too, it's all the same to them now."
^The boatmen are talking about the price of salt.

ch2_listen_boatmen: ^At the landing stage two boatmen were unloading a flat-bottomed boat and bickering under their breath.
^"...and I'm telling you, there are two levers at the sluice. A big one and a small one. The big one lifts the gate, the small one drains the chapel. Dwarves made it, not men."
^"One fellow did. The water went, he climbed in. Then the water came back, and he didn't. After that Renna had the small lever wrapped in chain so nobody'd play with it."
^"Go and look yourself. The chain's still hanging there."
^A note in the journal: "A small lever at the sluice, wrapped in chain."

b: ^Now it is clear where to look: the flooded chapel by the sluice. The small lever of the gate drains it.
^The chapel by the sluice. A dry stone floor, an empty altar.
^Next to the big gate lever there is a second, smaller one, wrapped in rusty chain. What it is for is unclear. Behind a grate in the wall stands black water.

ch2_hunt_site: ^The small lever was where they said: right by the gate, wrapped three times in chain. The chain had rusted so that the links had grown together.

b: ^Above the lever a rune was cut, just one. Not "hold", as above the gate. Another one. It took you a moment to make it out: "Release".

ch2_hunt_site: ^Garret cut through the chain with his cleaver on the third blow. Irena and Velior threw their weight on the lever together.
^Behind the grate something gurgled and hummed, and the water went down: slowly, squelching, baring steps.
^The steps led into a small hall with a low vault.

b: ^The chapel by the sluice. The candle on the altar still burns, the man in vestments still stands with his back to you, the spear in his hands.
^The chapel was tiny: six benches, an altar of rough stone, bands of silt on the walls right up to the vault. On the altar stood a candle.
^By the altar, with his back to you, stood a man in vestments heavy with water. In his hands he held a three-pronged fishing spear, long, taller than himself. He did not move.
^From somewhere under the floor, from the water that had not quite gone, came a barely audible: "The water remembers, the water never sleeps..."
^You did not know what it meant. Maybe nothing. Maybe in these mines all the songs about water are the same.

c-1: ^You stepped back to the stairs. The candle on the altar did not waver. Neither did the man by the altar.

ch2_hunt_meet: ^Water squelched underfoot. The man by the altar turned round.
^It was Father Meren. You understood that at once, though you had never seen him: this is how someone looks who served thirty years in one chapel and did not leave it even when the water came.
^Almost nothing was left of his face. The eyes were left, white as the fish of the underground lake.
^He took the candle from the altar and held it out towards you. The spear he held in his other hand, prongs down.
^"Who... has come..." he said. His voice was like gurgling in a pipe. "Living or... dead..."

b: ^You knew this rite. In the old parishes that was how they met those who came back from the mine after a cave-in: the candle does not go out only for the living.

c-1: ^"I don't know, Father," you said. And you were surprised yourself that it was true.

b: ^The candle flame bent away from you as if in a draught, and shrank to a blue point.
^The dead man looked at it for a long time. Then he raised the spear.
^"They all... say so..." He moved towards you. Slowly, the way one walks along the bottom. "The dead... into the water... I... pin them..."

ch2_hunt_alive: ^The flame leaned towards you and straightened. Even, yellow, warm.
^The dead man looked at it for a long time, as if remembering what it meant.

b: ^The candle flame trembled. It bent away from you, came back, bent away again. But it did not go out.
^"Honest..." said the dead man. "The dead... don't doubt... And you... still..."
^The flame leaned towards you and straightened.
^"The living... always... doubt," said the dead man, and in the gurgling there was something like a laugh.

ch2_hunt_gift: ^He set the candle on the altar and held out the spear to you. Shaft first, the way a post is handed over.
^"Pin them... into the water," he said. "So they don't rise."
^Then Father Meren lay down on the floor by the altar, the way one lies down to sleep, and moved no more. The candle burned a little longer and went out by itself.
^Irena knelt beside him and closed his eyes. What was left of them.
^"For thirty years he guarded them from the dead," she said. "And then he became one of the dead and guarded them still. Only he asked first."
^You took the spear. The shaft was wet and cold, and the prongs dry and warm, as if just taken out of a fire.
^Somewhere behind the wall the water hummed. It was time to go.
ch2_hunt_fight: ^Father Meren fell to his knees by the altar. The spear dropped from his hands and rang on the stone.
^"Didn't... pin you..." he said, almost surprised. "So... still... living."
^He lay down on the floor the way one lies down to sleep, and moved no more. The candle on the altar burned down and went out by itself.
^Irena did not go to him. She was looking at you.

b: ^"Many don't notice the difference," said Velior. Quietly, without his usual smirk.

ch2_hunt_fight: ^You picked up the spear. The shaft was wet and cold, and the prongs were cold too.
^Somewhere behind the wall the water hummed. It was time to go.

arches: ^Лестница кончилась залом, в котором мог бы уместиться весь Эшмур вместе с полем. Арки уходили вверх, в темноту, куда не доставал свет фонаря. Каждая была вырезана из цельной скалы, и на каждой — ряды угловатых рун.
^Здесь было сухо. И очень тихо: шаги не отдавались эхом, а будто проваливались в камень.

b: ^ у первой арки. Руны были те же, что на шлюзе, но здесь их было много, и они складывались в слова.
^— Я разбирал три знака из десяти. А ты читаешь, как с листа.
^Велиор провёл пальцами по рунам, шевеля губами.
^— Я знаю несколько знаков. «Молчать». «Спать». И вот этот, «он», но с каким-то хвостом, будто «он» — это не человек. — Он убрал руку. — Что-то вроде: «Здесь молчат, чтобы он спал».

arches: ^Ответить никто не успел. В нишах между арками что-то сдвинулось. Каменные фигуры в рост человека, с лицами без ртов, медленно повернули головы на звук голоса.

^Это была кузница. Дварфийская, огромная: горн размером с деревенский дом, наковальни, на которых мог бы спать человек, желоба для расплавленного металла, уходящие в стену.
^— Здесь можно жить, — сказала Ирена, оглядываясь. — Сухо, тепло, вода есть. И стены, которые простоят ещё тысячу лет.
^— Здесь можно держать оборону, — сказал Гаррет. Он думал о другом.
